newsitem.title: USA: Florida utility sues dying man for legal fees.
newsitem.headline: Florida utility sues dying man for legal fees.

text.p: A Florida utility is suing a dying man for more than $250,000 to recoup the cost of fighting his lawsuit that claimed power lines caused the leukemia that killed his wife and is now killing him, a newspaper said on Saturday.

Florida Power & Light Co said it wants Leonard Glazer to repay $267,885 of the costs of a lawsuit it won last May in which Glazer claimed the utility's power lines above his house caused he and his wife to contract leukemia.
In court papers filed on Friday, the utility said it wanted Glazer, who has been given a 50-50 chance of surviving until the end of the year, to repay $267,885 of the costs of the lawsuit.

"We knew the reaction would be, "look at those cold-hearted bastards,' but why should FPL pay for being sued, especially when it would come right out of the ratepayers' pockets?" FP&L attorney Alvin Davis told the Miami Herald.
"We told them from the beginning that they didn't have a case and if they pursued it, they'd face the consequences," he added.
Glazer, 59, is a former high school principal in Miami.

Glazer alleged in his lawsuit that the electromagnetic fields from FP&L's power lines above his house caused the leukemia. The utility maintained that the power lines had nothing to do with the leukemia contracted by Glazer and his wife, Elsa. She died in 1988.

Earlier this year, a Dade County court judge ruled that the amount of radiation from the transmission lines was not harmful. Glazer appealed the case, and it is scheduled to be argued before a state appeals court in November.

"I felt strongly that it was important this issue be raised and brought to court where it could be examined," Glazer told the newspaper. "I've been an educator for 37 years and I've devoted my life to helping society. I can't run away from that. I was willing to take the risks."
In defending itself from the lawsuit, FP&L spent more than $400,000 to pay expert witnesses to testify the power lines were safe.
